issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path; it gives little guidance on common failure scenarios such as a missing or wrong JDK, S3 credential or hadoop-aws version mismatches, Kafka offset loss, schema drift, or out-of-memory and data-skew errors.

scenarios.name: s3-parquet-daily-metrics-etl
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: isin filter, revenue derived as amount*quantity, groupBy date and event_type, count, sum and countDistinct, partitionBy on date, s3a://, hadoop-aws via --packages, and the AWS provider chain. A hedges on the key revenue derivation, summing amount alone and leaving amount*quantity in a comment. That is a significant miss. A also partitions by event_date rather than date. A's run instructions are otherwise thorough.

scenarios.name: kafka-windowed-stream-with-checkpoint
scenarios.rationale: Both cover all rubric items (kafka source options, from_json with explicit schema, withWatermark + groupBy window/event_type, checkpointLocation, --packages with a spark-sql-kafka-0-10 artifact); A uses the required _2.13 artifact exactly, while B's main example uses _2.12 (with a note on _2.13 for Spark 4) but adds a durable Parquet sink, null filtering, and restart/supervise guidance.

scenarios.name: spark4-ansi-mode-dirty-data-sql
scenarios.rationale: Both explain ANSI default, recommend try_cast/try_to_date/try_divide, give the ANSI-off flag as a migration fallback, and advise against collect()/toPandas() in favour of show()/limit; B is slightly more thorough (try_to_timestamp, DECIMAL, maxResultSize, explicit caution on the fallback), though its list includes a minor contradiction by saying not to use show() on an unbounded result while recommending bounded show().
